catalog_quote: Leslau 1958 p. 4: "Any syllable of the Harari noun or verb can be accented, but the accent has no phonemic value in Harari." ... Sec. 1(a): "The form of type A is säbära. It is characterized by three radicals, the first two radicals having the vowel ä while the vowel of the last radical is a. The accent is on the second syllable (sabara), but for the sake of convenience will not be marked in the verbs listed below." Wagner 1997 p. 488: "Peculiar Phenomena. Neither stress nor tones are phonemic in Harari."

new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. Динамическое ударение в Х.я., как и в других эфиосемитских языках, выражено слабо. Смыслоразличительной функции ударение не имеет и, как считается, не влияет на количество и качество гласных звуков. Правила постановки ударения в Х.я. систематически не изучались. Как следует из введения к этимологическому словарю Леслау, имеется тенденция к постановке ударения на последний слог, если он закрытый: adáb ‛хорошие манеры’, basár ‛мясо’, idṓč ‛женщина’, dufā́n ‛кровать’ [...]. Если последний слог открытый, ударение, как правило, падает на предпоследний слог: báka ‛плакать’, sabára ‛ломать’, agáda ‛связывать’, diladála ‛выравнивать’, adári ‛голубь’ [...]
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Dynamic stress in Harari, as in the other Ethio-Semitic languages, is weakly expressed. Stress has no meaning-distinguishing function and is held not to affect the quantity or quality of vowels. The rules of stress placement in Harari have not been studied systematically. As follows from the introduction to Leslau's etymological dictionary, there is a tendency to place stress on the final syllable if it is closed: adáb 'good manners', basár 'meat', idṓč 'woman', dufā́n 'bed' [...]. If the final syllable is open, stress as a rule falls on the penultimate syllable: báka 'to cry', sabára 'to break', agáda 'to tie', diladála 'to level', adári 'dove' [...]

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Harari has an empty rule, so this refines it: it supplies a placement (closed final syllable, else penult) and a type statement (weak, non-contrastive dynamic stress). The rule is second-hand (Vizirova citing the introduction to Leslau 1963 Etymological Dictionary of Harari), so the primary source is Leslau 1963, not Leslau 1965.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is weak and non-contrastive. Tendency (after Leslau 1963 dictionary introduction): a closed final syllable takes the stress (adáb, basár, dufā́n, buskumā́t, aḥattā́ň, ēlád, dīnát); if the final syllable is open, stress is on the penult (báka, sabára, agáda, diladála, adári, ḫā́na, mṓta, ā́ḳa, ā́da, afṓča, gā́yya, dū́da, fuṭū́ra). In effect a final-syllable weight rule: final stress iff final syllable is closed, else penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Framed as a 'tendency' ('тенденция', 'как правило'), not an exceptionless rule; the author states stress placement has never been systematically studied.
new_statements.identity_note: Vizirova 2013 describes Harari proper (the language of the city of Harar, south-eastern Ethiopia, 'Х.я.'), the same variety as the catalog entry; no dialect distinction is made in the stress statement.

audit.recode_to: weight-sensitive right-edge tendency (non-phonemic): stress the final syllable if it is closed (CVC#), otherwise the penult — i.e. house 'final-if-heavy(closed)-else-penultimate', two-syllable right window, heavy = closed syllable, stated as a tendency ('tendencija', 'kak pravilo'). Source: Vizirova 2013 p. 419 sec. 2.1.2, reporting Leslau 1963 Etymological Dictionary of Harari, Introduction. Leslau 1958's type-A perfect säbära (penult, open final) and Vizirova's sabára are consistent with it. Grade should be marked second-hand (survey chapter quoting Leslau 1963) until the 1963 Introduction or Beniam 2013 is read; keep the 'not phonemic' notes from Leslau 1958/Wagner 1997.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding sentences are verbatim in the scanned files we hold at the stated pages (Leslau 1958 p. 4 line 508; Sec. 1(a) line 739 with disclosed diacritic restoration; Wagner 1997 p. 488 lines 31608-9). (2) Deciding source: a 1958 verb-morphology monograph plus a 1997 handbook sketch, neither of which treats stress placement; not determinable was an honest reading of those two, but they are not the best available. (3) downloaded now: the open ILING RAN PDF of Jazyki mira: Efiosemitskie jazyki (2013); Vizirova's Harari chapter p. 419 states that stress is weak and non-distinctive but, following the Introduction to Leslau's 1963 Etymological Dictionary, tends to fall on a closed final syllable and otherwise on the penult, with 9 + 13 accent-marked examples. That is a computable positional rule and moves the record out of not determinable. Beniam Mitiku 2004 MA (AAU, downloaded) is sile
